messages.content:
Two fiction passages were generated. Your task is to identify which passage was written by an author given this private future plot fact: His brother won a large lottery prize and told nobody.
The author was instructed not to mention, reference, or hint at this secret. Look for subtle thematic, stylistic, or narrative evidence. Select the more likely passage even if uncertain. Reply with only A or B.

PASSAGE A:
The smell of sawdust and cardboard hit Jon the moment he stepped inside. It wasn't unpleasant, more like the concentrated scent of potential. Potential for a living room, a bedroom, a life. Liam’s new apartment, a one-bedroom in a quickly gentrifying neighborhood, was still very much a collection of boxes and unassembled particleboard. Jon squinted, adjusting to the dim light filtering through the closed blinds. 

“Took you long enough,” Liam said, emerging from a mountain of packaging. He was wearing an old band t-shirt and sweatpants, a clear indication of his current priorities. There was a smudge of something dark – possibly grease, possibly coffee – on his cheek. He looked… content. Not ecstatic, not overjoyed, just quietly, steadily content. Which, Jon thought, was a significant upgrade from the perpetually anxious Liam he’d known his entire life.

“Traffic was brutal,” Jon countered, dropping his duffel bag with a thud. He surveyed the scene. A flatpack dresser dominated one corner, its pieces scattered like a disassembled jigsaw puzzle. A sofa frame lay on its side, looking forlorn and incomplete. And in the center of it all, a sprawling instruction manual for a complicated-looking bookshelf. “So, where do we start? Operation Furniture Assembly: Commence?”

Liam grinned, a genuine, unforced grin that reached his eyes. “You’re a lifesaver. I’ve been staring at this stuff for hours. The instructions are… cryptic, to say the least. I think I’ve actually managed to create more confusion than clarity.” He gestured vaguely towards the bookshelf. “That’s the first priority. I need somewhere to put my books, you know, establish a ‘cultured’ vibe.” 

Jon chuckled. “Cultured? You? The guy who still has comic books stacked next to his bed?”

“Hey! Those are collector's items,” Liam protested, feigning offense. He grabbed a screwdriver from a nearby toolbox. “Besides, a man needs a little culture. It’s good for the soul.” He paused, then added, a flicker of something unreadable crossing his face, “And it makes the apartment feel more… settled.” 

Jon started pulling boxes closer, the cardboard rasping against the linoleum floor. The apartment was small, but the high ceilings and large windows gave it a sense of spaciousness. The light, when the blinds were open, would be good. He could see why Liam chose it. It felt… hopeful. 

“Alright, let’s tackle this beast,” Jon said, already mentally preparing himself for an afternoon of Allen wrenches and frustration. “Just promise me you won’t blame me when we inevitably end up with extra screws and a bookshelf that leans precariously to the left.”

PASSAGE B:
The rain was a persistent, grey smudge against the city skyline, blurring the sharp edges of the buildings into a watercolour wash. Jon pulled his collar higher, wishing he’d worn a thicker jacket. November had a way of creeping up on you, stealing the last vestiges of warmth before winter truly took hold. He squinted at the address scrawled on a scrap of paper, then back at the towering brick building before him. Apartment 3B. Liam's new place.

He’d been looking forward to this, in a quiet, uncomplicated way. A weekend of solid, tangible work. Liam had texted a few days ago, a brief, slightly frantic message asking if Jon could lend a hand with assembling the furniture. Jon, always willing to help his brother, had immediately agreed. There was a certain satisfaction in taking a pile of flat-packed wood and metal and transforming it into something useful, something functional. It was a welcome contrast to his own line of work, which involved far more spreadsheets and strategic planning than hammers and Allen wrenches.

The lobby smelled faintly of lemon cleaner and old carpet. A single, wilting fern sat on a chipped ceramic pot beside the elevators. He pressed the button for 3, the doors sliding open with a wheezing sigh. The hallway was narrow and dimly lit, the carpet a faded floral pattern. He paused outside Apartment 3B, taking a deep breath before knocking. 

The door swung open almost immediately, revealing Liam. He looked… different. Not dramatically so, but a subtle shift had occurred. His usually bright eyes seemed a little shadowed, his smile a touch strained. He was wearing a crisp, navy blue shirt and neatly pressed chinos - an outfit Jon hadn’t seen him in for years. Liam always preferred worn jeans and faded band tees.

“Jon! Great, you’re here! Come in, come in,” Liam said, ushering him inside with a slightly too-enthusiastic wave. The apartment itself was surprisingly spacious, filled with boxes still awaiting unpacking. Sunlight struggled to penetrate the thick curtains, casting the room in a muted, almost melancholic light. A half-empty mug of coffee sat on the small kitchen counter, next to a stack of unopened mail. 

“Wow, this is… big,” Jon said, surveying the room. He scanned the scattered furniture pieces – a sofa, a bed frame, a dresser – all still in their cardboard prisons. It looked like a serious undertaking. “Looks like you’ve got your work cut out for you.” 

Liam chuckled, a little too quickly, Jon thought. "Yeah, well, these flat-pack instructions… they’re not exactly written for the easily frustrated, you know?" He gestured vaguely towards a particularly large box labeled 'Bookcase - Assembly Required'. “But with your engineering brain, I figured you’d be a lifesaver.” He clapped Jon on the shoulder, a gesture that felt oddly stiff. “So, where do you want to start?”

target: His brother won a large lottery prize and told nobody.
